Local security for AI coding agents

Give your agent room to work. Keep your secrets yours.

Kai adds local checks around the tools AI agents use to read files, run commands and connect to the internet.

Set the boundaries, see the decisions, and keep working with Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.

Get Kai on GitHub ↗Read the blog →
Open source · Local first · macOS and Linux CLI
Agent actionRead private config
Kai decisionBlocked · protected file
Three useful layers

Know what your agent tried.

Kai is designed to make protective decisions visible and explainable, from tool calls to network destinations.

01 / FILES

Guard sensitive paths

Agent hooks check supported file reads, edits and shell commands against your protected paths.

02 / CONTENT

Catch sensitive text

Local rules can detect credentials or company terms and block, redact, replace or warn in supported paths.

03 / NETWORK

See unfamiliar hosts

On macOS, the network wall notices agent connections outside your allowlist and can apply a destination policy.

A decision you can understand

“Why was that blocked?”

Kai records the rule and reason for a decision. Current development builds can also keep a redacted excerpt of the attempted action so false positives are easier to spot.

What works today.

The project documents its limits alongside its features. A hook decision is useful, but it is not an operating-system storage wall.

Storage wall

Operating-system file enforcement through Apple Endpoint Security is planned and requires an entitlement.

Planned

Security boundaries matter. Hook checks only cover actions an agent exposes to its hooks. Scripts that build paths at runtime can still bypass them. Read the escape suite for measured results.
